method: Chromium, dark colour scheme, at 320, 390, 430, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 CSS pixels, by scripts/runtime/views_pass.js: Múcaro has one address and keeps its views in memory, so the scan loads '/', clicks each workspace view and measures it. The app's strict script policy was lifted for the test browser only so axe-core could be injected; the app itself was not changed.
result: No change needed for the targeted rules: zero axe violations of any impact, no horizontal overflow, no unnamed buttons, in all 49 view loads.
not_shown: Views were opened, not otherwise operated; empty workspace; controls under 24 px are recorded, not judged (WCAG 2.5.8 allows exceptions).

rescan_at_main.why: main added four workspaces after the first scan (GIS, OCR, Code, Artifacts; mucaro-ai 7f46464), so they had never been scanned.
rescan_at_main.method: Same as the first scan: fresh export of origin/main, frontend built, served by scripts/runtime/serve_snapshot.py, scanned by scripts/runtime/views_pass.js at the same seven widths with the script policy lifted in the test browser only.
rescan_at_main.rendered: Each new workspace became the current page and showed its own heading and description (GIS; OCR / page review; Code; Artifacts); the app was not in its locked state.
rescan_at_main.result: All 11 entries (10 workspaces and Background tasks) at 7 widths, 77 view loads: zero axe violations of any impact, no horizontal overflow, no unnamed buttons, no page errors. The four new workspaces are clean in this scan.
rescan_at_main.not_shown: Workspaces were opened, not operated. The new workspaces' result views appear only after an inspection is run (a GeoJSON layer, an image page, a repository check) and were not reached. A clean scan is not a screen-reader review.

results_scan.why: The rescan saw the four new workspaces empty; their result views render only after an inspection runs.

inspections.how: Through the UI, as mucaro-ai's qa/rendered/rendered_qa.mjs does: the input folders granted with POST /permissions/directories/grant, then in each workspace the request, Allow (bound to the arguments digest) and Run. All three were PENDING_APPROVAL, then EXECUTED.
inspections.gis: gis.inspect on backend/tests/fixtures/gis_corpus/usgs_pr_earthquakes_2020-01-06_2020-01-08.geojson: coordinate system EPSG:4326, features table of 30 rows, bounding-box preview.
inspections.ocr: ocr.analyze_image on a generated 900x260 PNG with two printed lines, read by Tesseract 5.3.4 (installed in the test container): 7 words, 'municipio de ponce informe de prueba 2026'.
inspections.code: coding.repo_status on a throwaway git repository: branch main, working tree dirty, untracked notes.txt.
inspections.artifacts: After the inspections and one chat turn (mock model): 2 inspection reports and 1 saved answer listed.

results_scan.method: scripts/runtime/views_pass.js unchanged, same settings as rescan_at_main (seven widths, phone widths through the menu, script policy lifted in the test browser only), run after the inspections so each workspace shows its results.
results_scan.result_views_present: At 320, 390 and 1280 px: gis-result, gis-features (30 rows) and gis-bbox-preview; ocr-result; code-repo-result; 2 artifact-report and 1 artifact-answer. No horizontal overflow in any.
results_scan.result: With results showing, all 11 entries at 7 widths, 77 view loads: zero axe violations of any impact, no overflow, no unnamed buttons, no page errors.
results_scan.not_shown: One inspection per workspace with small inputs; long or failing results (an OCR engine error, a large layer) were not seen. Results were displayed, not operated (raw-result toggles, exports). Not a screen-reader review.
